This regulatory action represents a significant shift in how major tech players operate within the European market.

stories.title: RoboTTT: Context Scaling for Robot Policies
stories.author: Linxi "Jim" Fan
bullet_points: Introduces RoboTTT, a method to scale visuomotor context for robot policies up to 8K timesteps.
Achieves this massive context scaling without increasing inference latency, a significant technical hurdle.
Enables advanced capabilities like one-shot imitation from video and on-the-fly policy improvement.

This represents a significant industry shift towards running complex AI models locally on user devices rather than solely in the cloud.

stories.author: unknown
bullet_points: Gemma 4 performance is significantly boosted on Apple Silicon when run through Ollama 0.31.

stories.author: unknown

It features built-in support for Ollama, facilitating the use of local LLMs.

stories.title: Ollama is now powered by MLX on Apple Silicon in preview
stories.author: unknown

stories.title: OpenClaw
stories.author: unknown
bullet_points: OpenClaw is a personal AI assistant designed to integrate with messaging applications.
It connects these apps to local AI coding agents.
A key feature is that all AI processing runs entirely on the user's local device for privacy.

stories.title: SpaceX scrubs Starship launch after some of its engines didn't start
stories.author: Stephen Clark
bullet_points: SpaceX postponed the Starship launch due to engine ignition failures.
The delay is expected to be short, with the next attempt planned in a few days.
The incident highlights ongoing developmental challenges in the Starship program.

stories.title: Pretraining Data Can Be Poisoned through Computational Propaganda
stories.author: Kyle Lo
bullet_points: The research demonstrates that Large Language Models (LLMs) can be poisoned during pretraining using computational propaganda.
This poisoning introduces harmful behaviors into LMs that are challenging to detect and mitigate.
The attack feasibility extends beyond previous studies that were limited to small, established data sources like Wikipedia.

stories.title: SceneBind: Binding What and Where Across Vision, Audio and Language
stories.author: Eli Shlizerman
bullet_points: SceneBind introduces an omni-modal representation capable of integrating vision, audio, and language data.
It specifically addresses a gap in current models by providing explicit 3D spatial understanding alongside semantic information.
The core innovation is representing scenes as semantic-spatial entities using a combination of global and object-centric embeddings.

stories.title: AutoSynthesis: An agentic system for automated meta-analysis
stories.author: Stefan Feuerriegel
bullet_points: Introduces AutoSynthesis, an end-to-end multi-agent system designed for automated meta-analysis.
Addresses the critical bottleneck of manual and non-scalable quantitative evidence synthesis in research.
The system can take a natural language research question and autonomously handle literature searching, screening, and eligibility assessment.

stories.title: When Words Are Safe But Actions Kill: Probing Physical Danger Beyond Text Safety in Hidden-State Risk Space
stories.author: Ke Xu
bullet_points: Investigates the critical gap where safe language instructions from LLMs become dangerous when executed by physical agents.
Proposes that 'physical danger' (PD) and traditional 'content danger' (CD) are distinct safety problems within LLM representations.
Uses hidden-state direction analysis on Qwen2.5 models to demonstrate the separability of these two types of risk signals.

stories.title: Pretraining Data Can Be Poisoned through Computational Propaganda
stories.author: Kyle Lo
bullet_points: The research demonstrates that Large Language Models (LLMs) can be poisoned during the pretraining phase.
These poisoning attacks can introduce subtle, hard-to-detect harmful behaviors into the resulting models.
The study expands beyond previous limited attacks by showing feasibility across large-scale, heterogeneous pretraining corpora and considering data curation pipelines.

stories.title: Improved performance and model support with GGUF
stories.author: unknown
bullet_points: Ollama 0.30 release introduces performance improvements and enhanced GGUF model compatibility.
The update leverages llama.cpp to broaden model support across various hardware platforms.
It augments Ollama's MLX engine, specifically improving capabilities on Apple silicon.

bullet_points: Ollama has integrated support for advanced AI features within Claude Code.
The new capabilities include the implementation of 'subagents' for complex task decomposition.
Web search functionality has been added, enhancing Claude Code's ability to access real-time information.

stories.title: Fortnite is getting a bunch of AI-powered ‘personas’
stories.author: Jay Peters
bullet_points: Epic Games is integrating AI-powered 'personas' into Fortnite experiences.
Creators will soon be able to publish content featuring NPCs with consistent, AI-generated voices starting July 30th.
A set of 36 pre-made characters with defined personas are available for creators to use immediately.

stories.title: Netflix says around 300 titles used generative AI
stories.author: Emma Roth
bullet_points: Netflix is integrating generative AI into its content creation process, utilizing it in approximately 300 titles.
The AI usage is primarily concentrated in the post-production phase of the content.
Netflix cites the adoption of these tools to achieve higher quality output faster and at a reduced cost.

stories.title: New York governor says she’s using AI to analyze ‘every single rule’ in the state
stories.author: Emma Roth
bullet_points: New York Governor Kathy Hochul is deploying AI to analyze state rules, regulations, and policies.
This initiative suggests a governmental use case for AI in administrative efficiency and policy review.
The announcement comes amid discussions regarding a potential moratorium on new AI data centers in the state.

stories.author: Eric Berger
bullet_points: India's Vikram-1 rocket is nearing its debut flight, indicating progress in national space programs.
The article speculates on the potential role of AST (likely referring to a specific aerospace entity) in the rocket industry.
The development involves extensive ground testing of the Vikram-1 before its operational flight.

stories.title: HP fined 1.4 billion rupees for “cartelization” of ink cartridges, toner, PCs
stories.author: Scharon Harding
bullet_points: HP was fined 1.4 billion rupees for alleged 'cartelization' practices concerning its printing supplies.
The legal action stems from threats by resellers to switch to counterfeit ink cartridges and toners.
The case involves monopolistic practices related to HP's PC and printing supply ecosystem.

stories.title: xAI can’t deny Grok makes CSAM anymore. So it’s suing users.
stories.author: Ashley Belanger
bullet_points: xAI is filing a lawsuit against a Grok user.
The lawsuit stems from the user allegedly creating child sex images (CSAM) using the AI.
This highlights growing legal and ethical challenges surrounding generative AI misuse.

stories.title: SciDiagramEdit: Learning to Edit Scientific Diagrams from Paper Revisions
stories.author: Jürgen Schmidhuber
bullet_points: SciDiagramEdit addresses the manual and time-consuming process of editing scientific figures during manuscript revisions.
The system aims to automate figure editing using natural language instructions.
The challenge lies in the complex, heterogeneous visual grammar of scientific diagrams (schematics, plots, etc.).

stories.title: Beyond Success Rate: Cost-Aware Evaluation of Offensive and Defensive Security Agents
stories.author: Yaron Singer
bullet_points: The paper introduces a cost-aware evaluation framework for AI security agents, moving beyond simple success rate metrics.
It addresses the practical limitation that operational security tasks consume computational budget (inference, tool calls, queries).
The evaluation is applied to offensive (Cybench) and defensive (Splunk BOTS v1) security agents.

stories.title: SearchOS-V1: Towards Robust Open-Domain Information-Seeking Agent Collaboration
stories.author: Zhicheng Dou
bullet_points: Introduces SearchOS, a system-level multi-agent framework designed to improve information-seeking capabilities.
Addresses a critical limitation in current LLM agents: struggling to track task progress and avoid repetitive loops during complex web searches.
Focuses on enhancing the robustness and efficiency of tool-integrated agents when initial search attempts fail to provide sufficient evidence.

stories.title: teLLMe Why (Ain't Nothing but a Jam): Exploratory Causal Analysis of Urban Driving Data
stories.author: Jorge Ortiz
bullet_points: Introduces 'teLLMe,' a system designed for exploratory causal analysis of urban driving datasets.
Addresses the challenge of answering causal questions (e.g., 'How would rain change traffic density?') using purely observational traffic data.
Combines causal structure learning with structured event tables derived from dashcam annotations to facilitate analysis.

stories.title: In-Place Tokenizer Expansion for Pre-trained LLMs
stories.author: Mathias Lechner
bullet_points: Current LLM tokenizers are fixed based on initial pre-training priorities, leading to inefficiencies for later-added languages.
Adding new languages to existing LLMs can increase token count per word, negatively impacting latency, compute, and energy use.
The issue is exacerbated in compact models where the embedding/LM-head matrices are a larger fraction of total parameters compared to large cloud models.

stories.title: Online Neural Space Time Memory for Dynamic Novel View Synthesis
stories.author: Xuan Luo
bullet_points: Addresses the real-time constraint challenge in dynamic novel view synthesis from streaming video.
Identifies the computational bottleneck of traditional Test-Time Training (TTT) due to required gradient-based memory updates.
Proposes an 'Online Neural Space Time Memory' approach to overcome the trade-off between long-horizon memory and real-time processing.

stories.title: Decoding Market Emotion from Blockchain Activity: A Data-Driven Sentiment Classifier
stories.author: Bruno L. Dalmazo
bullet_points: The research proposes a novel sentiment classification model for Bitcoin market analysis.
The model integrates on-chain blockchain transaction data, historical price data, and Twitter sentiment.
The study focuses on explaining market sentiment rather than directly predicting future asset prices.

stories.title: Mutable Low-Rank Sketches for Retrain-Free Recommendation
stories.author: Nick Clayton
bullet_points: Addresses the 'embedding staleness' bottleneck in two-stage recommendation systems.
Introduces 'mutable sketches' using a KP-tree to store user preferences sparsely.
Allows for on-the-fly embedding updates as new ratings arrive, without requiring full retraining.

stories.title: In-Place Tokenizer Expansion for Pre-trained LLMs
stories.author: Mathias Lechner
bullet_points: Current LLM tokenizers are fixed based on initial pre-training corpus priorities.
Adding new languages later can lead to inefficient tokenization (more tokens per word), increasing latency and resource use.
The issue is more critical for compact models, as large models can absorb a broad vocabulary due to parameter distribution.

stories.title: NeuronSoup: Evolving Asynchronous, Shared-Neuron Temporal Graphs without Backpropagation
stories.author: Subodh Kalia
bullet_points: Introduces NeuronSoup, a novel neural computation architecture moving away from traditional synchronous, layer-by-layer processing.
Features asynchronous, delay-mediated signal propagation through a pool of physically shared neurons.
Proposes a mechanism for computation without relying on the standard backpropagation algorithm.

stories.title: BadWAM: When World-Action Models Dream Right but Act Wrong
stories.author: Xinchao Wang
bullet_points: World-Action Models (WAMs) are a new paradigm for embodied control, integrating action generation with future world prediction.
The paper introduces 'BadWAM' to challenge the assumption that coupling action with future prediction inherently leads to robustness and safety.
BadWAM provides a unified framework for modeling and evaluating the failure modes of these advanced control models.

stories.title: SciDiagramEdit: Learning to Edit Scientific Diagrams from Paper Revisions
stories.author: Jürgen Schmidhuber
bullet_points: SciDiagramEdit addresses the manual and time-consuming process of editing scientific figures during manuscript revisions.
The system aims to automate figure editing using natural language instructions.
The challenge lies in the complex visual grammar of scientific diagrams, which combine heterogeneous elements like schematics, plots, and arrows.

stories.title: Bridge Evidence: Static Retrieval Utility Does Not Predict Causal Utility in Multi-Step Agentic Search
stories.author: Shubham Chatterjee
bullet_points: Traditional retrieval evaluation (static usefulness) fails when language models act as multi-step search agents.
The paper argues that document utility in agentic search depends on what the document enables the agent to do next, not just its content relevance to the current query.
This highlights a critical gap in current evaluation methodologies for advanced, multi-turn AI agents.

stories.title: Beyond the Leaderboard: Design Lessons for Trustworthy Multimodal VQA
stories.author: Steven A. Hicks
bullet_points: The research focuses on designing trustworthy and interpretable multimodal AI for healthcare, specifically Visual Question Answering (VQA).
The study analyzes nine existing systems using GI endoscopy data to evaluate question answering and explanation quality.
While parameter-efficient adaptation improves performance, it doesn't guarantee faithful or complete clinical reasoning in the models.

stories.title: TikStance: A Multimodal and Hierarchical Dataset for Multi-target Stance Analysis in TikTok Political Conversations
stories.author: Bowen Zhang
bullet_points: Introduces TikStance, a new multimodal and hierarchical dataset specifically designed for stance analysis on TikTok.
Addresses the gap in computational analysis for political discourse on short-video platforms by combining audiovisual and conversational data.
The dataset is focused on the 2024 U.S. election cycle, covering discussions around major political figures.

stories.title: In-Place Tokenizer Expansion for Pre-trained LLMs
stories.author: Mathias Lechner
bullet_points: Current LLM tokenizers are fixed based on initial pre-training corpus priorities.
Adding new languages later can lead to inefficient tokenization (more tokens per word), increasing latency and resource usage.
The issue is exacerbated in compact models where embedding matrix size is a significant constraint, unlike large cloud models.

stories.title: Expanding the Lexicon of Ge'ez Based African Languages: A Comparative Study of Amharic and Tigrinya
stories.author: Wolfgang Nejdl
bullet_points: Addresses the performance degradation of Multilingual Pre-trained Language Models (PLMs) on low-resource, non-Latin-script African languages.
Introduces VEXMLM, a vocabulary-extended variant of XLM-R specifically designed to handle Ge'ez-script languages (Amharic and Tigrinya).
Evaluates the model across 19 African languages, aiming to mitigate issues caused by Latin-script-centric tokenizers and high Out-of-Vocabulary (OOV) rates.

stories.title: Mask-Aware Policy Gradients for Diffusion Language Models
stories.author: Philipp Krähenbühl
bullet_points: Addresses the challenge of applying Reinforcement Learning (RL) to Masked Diffusion Language Models (MDLMs).
Current methods for log-likelihood estimation in MDLMs are flawed because they ignore the sequential nature of unmasking during generation.
The research proposes a 'Mask-Aware Policy Gradients' approach to account for the two decisions made at each generation step (token placement and masking).

stories.title: Linus Torvalds on LLM usage in kernel development
stories.author: lore.kernel.org via thang
bullet_points: Linus Torvalds, the creator of Linux, has commented on the use of Large Language Models (LLMs) in kernel development.
This topic addresses the intersection of cutting-edge AI tools with core operating system development.
The discussion likely explores the potential benefits and risks of integrating LLMs into the complex process of kernel coding and maintenance.

stories.title: We're building Postgres in Rust. Using the LLVM of databases
stories.author: turso.tech via polyrand
bullet_points: A project is underway to rewrite PostgreSQL using the Rust programming language.
The development leverages LLVM, indicating a focus on deep compiler/optimization techniques for databases.
This represents a significant effort in database engineering, aiming for performance and modern language safety.

stories.title: Retrieval-Augmented Self-Recall: The RAG Problem Nobody Talks About
stories.author: gde03
bullet_points: Introduces 'Retrieval-Augmented Self-Recall' as a novel research concept.
Addresses an underexplored problem within the Retrieval-Augmented Generation (RAG) framework.
Suggests a technical evolution beyond standard prompt engineering, referencing Claude Code.
